I1.quote: Searched the whole article (text layer and page images, pp. 1963-1972) for a gravimetric, volumetric (Sieverts) or flow measurement of the amount of H2 taken up. None found: hydrogen adsorption is followed only through the e.s.r. signal height h and its change Delta-h, given in arbitrary units (Fig. 7, Fig. 8, eqn (9)-(12)); no amount adsorbed (wt%, mmol/g, cm3 STP/g) is measured. The only electrochemical step (Table 1) determines platinum coverage, not H2 uptake.

notes: Research article (J. Chem. Soc., Faraday Trans. 1, 1978), not a review; record is_retracted false and no retraction statement in the PDF; no statement that the data were published before. The I1 failure is coded no_conditions_stated: the work is experimental (not theoretical_only) and the H2 is gas-phase (not electrochemical). Evidence that the only H2 response is an e.s.r. intensity: 'Δh is the change in the intensity induced by the introduction of hydrogen gas and is assumed to be proportional to the coverage θ of hydrogen' (main, p. 8, journal p. 1970) and Fig. 7 caption 'h values are in arbitrary units' (main, p. 9, journal p. 1971). For a resolver: had I1 been met, the sorbent is 0-0.6 wt% Pt on graphite (carbon majority), conditions 0-100 C and 5-700 Torr are stated, and a supplier surface area is given: 'spectroscopically pure powder (SP-1, 200mesh, surface area 2 m2 g-1, Union Carbide)' (main, p. 2, journal p. 1964, Experimental, Catalyst).
